result.summary: JMAK now accepts commands over TCP and SMS. A new JmakProtocolEncoder builds the TCP form ($id;value;|...#, returned as ASCII bytes) or the SMS form (JMAK#action;id;value#...#, with JMAK#REBOOT# for reboot). JmakProtocol declares the same 12 commands for data and text and registers the encoder on both channels. The fast gate passes: Checkstyle is clean and the full unit suite runs 613 tests with 0 failures and 27 skips, all from existing @Disabled annotations. Nothing was committed or pushed.

changes.summary: New encoder extending StringProtocolEncoder, constructor (Protocol, boolean textChannel). Maps each command to parameters (ids 2, 12, 13, 16, 17, 30, 34, 43, 55, 57, 59, 93, 94, 167). TCP output is $id;value;|...# and is returned as an ASCII ByteBuf. SMS output is JMAK#action;id;value#...# with JMAK#REBOOT# for reboot. Custom returns the data as given. Output control maps index 1/2/3 to 34/94/167 and returns null for other indexes. Set connection uses param 13 for an IPv4 address and 43 otherwise, then param 12 for the port.

Declares the 12 supported commands for data and text (custom included), sets the SMS encoder with textChannel=true, and adds the TCP encoder with textChannel=false to the TCP pipeline. StringEncoder is not added: the encoder emits bytes itself.
Adds TYPE_ALARM_MOVEMENT = "alarmMovement" for the movement alarm command, since no movement alarm type existed.

New tests: testEncodeTcp (every command over TCP, plus an unsupported output index returning null), testEncodeSms (every command over SMS, including JMAK#REBOOT# and custom), and testEncodeTcpPipeline (the encoder run after NetworkMessageHandler, as in production).
Adds a 2026-11-02 entry: what changed, what was learned about the TCP pipeline, and what is left open, as AGENTS.md requires.

acceptance.criterion: Commands are encoded as described over TCP ($id;value;|...# format, the set connection example $43;jmak.com.br;|12;5259;#, reboot $93;1;#, and so on).

Run via make test TESTS='org.traccar.protocol.Jmak*Test': 5 tests, 0 failures.

acceptance.criterion: Commands are encoded as described over SMS (JMAK#action;id;value#...# format, the examples JMAK#s;34;1#, JMAK#s;13;191.233.246.121#s;12;5259#, JMAK#e;57;0#, and the literal JMAK#REBOOT#).
acceptance.evidence: JmakProtocolEncoderTest.testEncodeSms passes; it asserts JMAK#s;34;1#, JMAK#s;34;0#, JMAK#s;94;1#, JMAK#s;2;120#, JMAK#s;30;1500#, JMAK#s;13;191.233.246.121#s;12;5259#, JMAK#s;43;jmak.com.br#s;12;5259#, JMAK#REBOOT#, JMAK#e;16;1#s;17;80#, JMAK#e;57;0#, JMAK#e;55;1#, JMAK#e;59;0#, and custom passthrough.

acceptance.criterion: The encoder class is org.traccar.protocol.JmakProtocolEncoder with constructor (Protocol protocol, boolean textChannel), and it is registered for data and text in the JMAK protocol.
acceptance.evidence: JmakProtocolEncoder.java declares the constructor. JmakProtocol.java calls setTextCommandEncoder(new JmakProtocolEncoder(this, true)), adds new JmakProtocolEncoder(JmakProtocol.this, false) to the TCP pipeline, and calls setSupportedDataCommands and setSupportedTextCommands with the same list.

acceptance.criterion: The change is covered by tests.
acceptance.evidence: JmakProtocolEncoderTest has three tests: testEncodeTcp, testEncodeSms and testEncodeTcpPipeline. The pipeline test runs NetworkMessageHandler plus the encoder and asserts ASCII bytes. The existing JmakProtocolDecoderTest and JmakFrameDecoderTest still pass.

acceptance.criterion: The existing test suite still passes.

The skips come from existing @Disabled annotations. I did not measure a pre-change baseline, so I cannot confirm the exact count delta; docs/harness/log.md records 612 from an earlier run.

human_needed.question: Is power removal alarm correctly mapped to the existing Command.TYPE_ALARM_REMOVE ("alarmRemove") for param 55? That type is used by the Watch protocol for a device-removal alarm, so the name may not match the intended meaning.
human_needed.why: The spec names a power removal alarm but no command type for it. I reused alarmRemove, which needs a human check or a dedicated type.

human_needed.question: Is it acceptable to add a new command type Command.TYPE_ALARM_MOVEMENT = "alarmMovement"? It is visible through the API's command types list and the web UI.
human_needed.why: No movement alarm command type existed, so I added one. This changes a shared model class and the public list of command types.

human_needed.question: What unit does the set odometer value (param 30) use: kilometres or metres? The decoder reads KEY_ODOMETER from km and multiplies by 1000, but the encoder sends the command data unchanged.
human_needed.why: The spec gives no conversion. If the device expects km and the user sends metres, the value would be wrong.

harness_gaps.problem: The log's test count (612) does not match the count now (613) after adding three test methods, and I had no pre-change baseline to explain the difference. No gate or script records the baseline.

The skill covers encoders only as a one-line step ('setSupportedDataCommands'). It does not warn that the TCP pipeline's NetworkMessageHandler unwraps the message before StringEncoder can encode it, which I only found by testing. A note on encoder output type (ByteBuf for TCP, String for SMS) would have saved time.

The task's start commit (99264cbd0) removed a JMAK encoder that the earlier commit d5124e7f5 had added, so the history contains a prior implementation of this exact feature. I looked only at the stat, did not read or reuse the removed code, and designed from the spec and the repo's own encoders.

The TCP command prefix in the task text is garbled: the literal prefix is replaced by the sentence 'You are working in a software repository. Do the following task.' The examples show '$', so I used '$' as the prefix. This should be confirmed.
